slackGuide.title: How Slack memory works
slackGuide.subtitle: What Cognee reads from Slack, where it goes, and how to ask it questions.
slackGuide.whatReadsBody: Messages and threads from the channels it has been switched on for, and nothing else. Switching a channel on also reads the history it already has, not just new messages. Private channels are only available once you invite Cognee into them; it cannot see a private channel it is not a member of.
slackGuide.switchingOnBody: Type /invite @cognee in the channel. It starts reading that channel straight away and posts a message saying so, where everyone in the channel can see it. You can also tick channels on the Integrations page; the two do the same thing.
slackGuide.whereEndsBody: Two knowledge bases per Slack workspace. Everything read from channels goes into slack-<your team id>; anything somebody deliberately remembers goes into slack-<your team id>-remembered, kept apart so removing one of those can never take a channel's history with it. Both are in Knowledge bases alongside the ones you build yourself, and questions search all of them.
slackGuide.whoCanAskBody: Anyone in this Cognee workspace. That is the part worth pausing on before switching a channel on: a message in that channel becomes answerable for every member, so treat switching on #hr or #compensation as publishing it to the whole team.
slackGuide.howToAskBody: Type /cognee-recall in any Slack channel, or mention @cognee with your question. The answer is ephemeral, so only you see it, and it does not post into the channel — there is a button if you want to share it. You can ask the same thing from Search in this app.
slackGuide.rememberOneBody: Pick Remember in Cognee from a message's ⋯ menu to keep that message deliberately, rather than relying on it being swept up with the rest of the channel. It gets a ✅ so the channel can see what is being kept. /cognee-remember does the same for something Slack never saw — a decision from a call, say. Forget in Cognee removes it again, and the ✅ comes off.
slackGuide.switchingOffBody: Remove Cognee from the channel, or untick it on the Integrations page. Either stops it reading anything new. What was already read stays searchable: entities pulled out of those messages may be referenced by other memory, so removing them is not a clean undo.
slackGuide.needsReconnectBody: Slack has stopped accepting the connection, usually because the app was removed from the workspace or its token expired. The install is still there and nobody disconnected it, so the fix is Reconnect rather than Connect: it is the same authorization step, and it keeps the channels you already selected. Nothing new is read until you do it.
slackGuide.whoControlsBody: One Slack workspace connects to one Cognee workspace, and only the Cognee workspace owner can connect or disconnect it. Channels are different: anyone in Slack who can invite the bot into a channel can switch that channel on, which is why it announces itself in the channel when it starts. The Integrations page is where you see every channel that is on, and untick any of them.

agent.allSetDescription: The loop you just saw — upload, exit, reopen, and your agent still remembers — is the whole point. Here’s why it works:
agent.lifeCycle: The Cognee plugin hooks into your agent’s lifecycle — no curl or manual API calls — and captures your session as you work.
agent.sessionEnd: When a session ends, it consolidates that session into your Cognee Cloud knowledge graph.
agent.newSession: On every new session, it automatically recalls your memory back from the cloud.
agent.why: That’s why, after running /exit and reopening, your agent still knew what you uploaded — sessions are disposable; your memory isn’t.
